chapter: My Mother's Account Book Bites Back.
subtitle: 我娘的账本会咬人
sentences: There was no earth-shattering secret letter inside the wooden chest.

Just six boat tickets, two delivery receipts, a letter so worn it was almost falling apart, and a daybook with its corners rubbed white. It wasn't much to look at. Still, Mother had Chuntao shut the doors tight before bringing over a lamp herself.
"Look at this first."
The top ticket read: Eighteenth day of the eleventh month. Dongping Wharf. Transported by the Jiang Trading House. Eight thousand shi of relief grain bound for Beihe.
It bore the Jiang Trading House's seal, along with what appeared to be the signature Wen Li's father had used when overseeing shipments as county magistrate.
Wen Li held the ticket and traced her father's name with the pad of her thumb.
"It's genuine," she said.
I glanced at her. "How can you be sure?"
"That's his handwriting."
But Mother took the paper back. "It looks like his writing. That doesn't make it proof. Someone could have copied it. We'd have to check the original register and hear what he has to say himself."
That startled me.
Not because she was being careful, but because she'd clearly considered the possibility that these papers might one day be examined.
"Then what about the ninth day of the twelfth month?" I asked.

Mother spread a delivery receipt beside it. The paper had yellowed. Across the middle were the words Three thousand shi received at the government granary. There was no receiving officer's name beneath them, only a blurred warehouse stamp.
"Eight thousand shipped out, but only three thousand received?"

"All I know is that the paper Accountant Song brought back says three thousand," Mother said. "Whether the granary actually received that amount is another matter. We'd need its records. This scrap of paper can't tell us where the other five thousand went."
She handed me the old letter.

Accountant Song's handwriting was crooked. He wrote that, after the boats arrived, someone had ordered him to enter the remaining grain under a separate account. He refused and was told to collect his transport fee and stop asking questions. Near the end, his writing almost gave out. Someone, he said, had begun asking about his grandson.
When I reached that part, I remembered how Chuntao had dragged me along by the hand as we ran.
In the novel, it was just an "old case." For the people caught up in it, it meant three years of never sleeping soundly.
"Did you report it to the authorities?" I asked.
"Accountant Song went to the county office," Mother said. "He came back with bruises on his face. When he wanted to take it to the prefectural office, I stopped him."
"Why?"
"Because his grandson was only six."
Her voice was firm, but she smoothed the letter flat twice.
Wen Li had been silent until then. At last she said quietly, "My father was taken away the following autumn because of that shipment. The case was later passed up to the Ministry of Punishments."
"What did he have to do with it?" I asked.

"The officials accused him of failing to oversee the delivery. Then they produced a warehouse receipt supposedly signed by him, confirming that all eight thousand shi had arrived. Somehow, the missing five thousand ended up being blamed on him."
"But did he sign the paper that said all eight thousand had been received?"
Wen Li looked at me, as though she hadn't expected me to ask.
"He did," she said. "My father admitted the signature was his. But he said he hadn't signed of his own free will."
"A signature is still a signature," Mother cut in. "He'll have to explain why he put his name to it."
Wen Li lowered her head. "I understand."
I'd expected her to defend her father. Instead, she didn't argue at all.
The room felt too stifling to sit still, so I opened the daybook. Two pages in, I found figures even stranger than the warehouse receipt.
"Mother, why are there two payments for transport?"
The first was an ordinary fee for hiring boats to carry grain. The second listed no boat number at all. Someone had written a tiny character beside it: Other.
Mother reached across and closed the book.
"Leave that entry alone for now."
I froze.
"Why?"
"Because I haven't worked out how to tell you about it."

She offered no further explanation, and even Wen Li had the sense not to press her. But I remembered exactly where the entry was. Mother's fear that the Jiangs might be held responsible hadn't come from nowhere.

Wen Li took out the notes she'd made from the marquis's private accounts. She pointed to the date in the twelfth month, then tapped the Jiang boat ticket. "At the very least, these dates don't match. But we still can't say they refer to the same voyage. Next we need the departure register from Dongping Wharf and the names of whoever received the grain at the government granary."
"Would records that old still exist?" I asked.
"That depends on who kept them," Mother said. "Accountant Song mentioned someone named Yan Mancang. He was the keeper of the old granary at Beihe. He might know where the five thousand shi went."
I sprang to my feet. "Then let's find him now!"
Mother gave me a sideways look. "Do you know where he lives?"
"No."
"Do you know if he's even alive?"
"No."
"Do you know who's watching the Jiang residence?"
"...No. Not that either."
"Then sit down."
I sat back down.
Wen Li lowered her head. Her shoulders gave a tiny shake.
"What are you laughing at?" I demanded.
"I'm not laughing."
"You're about to burst out laughing!"
"I only think Madam Jiang has made an excellent point."
I turned to Mother for support. Instead, she pushed a teacup toward me. "Have some water. You've talked quite enough for one day."
Since when had those two ended up on the same side?
By evening, we hadn't gone straight after Yan Mancang. Instead, we went to a hauling agency that had worked with the Jiangs for years.
Mother sent Uncle Qin, the family's longtime steward, with us. He carried a list of the boatmen hired back then and said we should start by asking their families.

I'd been wondering whether a bag of silver might buy us an answer. Uncle Qin brought me firmly back to earth. "Miss, if the Xie family is looking for this man too, and you start throwing money around, the whole city will know whom you're after by tomorrow."
"Then what do we do?"
"Find the agency he worked through and speak to the old hands there. We'll say we've come to settle some unpaid wages."
Wen Li glanced at me. "You could learn a thing or two."
I bristled. "I'm the one paying. You're the one talking. Why do you get to teach me?"
"Because money makes too much noise."
I couldn't help laughing. Then I felt a little ashamed. She'd put her finger on a danger I hadn't even considered.

There were two old workers at the agency. One said Yan Mancang had left Beihe the year before. The other had seen him looking for work at the Cen family's hauling agency in the south of the city, though he didn't know if the man was still there.
Uncle Qin silently committed the lead to memory. Outside, a child selling sugar figures accidentally dropped a bamboo stick by my feet.
I was about to bend down and pick it up when Wen Li caught my wrist.
Two men stood across the street. Their clothes were the plain, short outfits worn by laborers, but looked suspiciously new for men who worked hauling freight. Neither took his eyes off us.
"The Xie family's men?" I whispered.
"Possibly," Wen Li said. "But we can't be sure."

She bent to return the bamboo stick to the child, bought a sugar figure, and handed it to me as though nothing were wrong. When the men saw that we weren't going farther, they slowly split up. One headed north. The other stayed at the mouth of the alley.
"What now?" I asked.
"We go back."
"We're giving up on Yan Mancang?"
"No." Wen Li glanced at the address Uncle Qin had found. "We send someone else. If we head straight south now, we'll lead those men right to him."

I thought back to the moment I'd arrived in this world and assumed that knowing the plot would solve everything. Suddenly, I felt foolish. Everyone here had to make decisions with whatever information they could get. Wen Li was no different.
When we returned to the Jiang residence, the gatekeeper handed me an invitation edged in gold.
It was written in Xie Linzhou's own hand.
Tomorrow at noon. The flower hall at the marquis's residence. Bring the Jiang Trading House's old accounts.
He'd added one more line at the bottom: Do not trust Wen Li again.
I stared at it, then looked up at Mother. "He says to bring the old accounts."
She didn't reach for the invitation. "How does he know I still have them?"
This time, not even Wen Li smiled.
We'd spent half the day behind closed doors trying to protect a secret. Apparently, someone else had been keeping count of it all along.
translations: 木匣里没有什么惊天动地的密信。
六张船票，两张收货凭单，一封快被翻烂的信，外加一本边角磨白的流水账。东西不多，李氏却让春桃把门关严，又亲手搬了盏灯过来。
“你们先看这个。”
最上面一张船票写着：十一月十八日，东平码头，姜记承运，北河赈粮八千石。
落款处有姜记商号的印，也有温父当年任知县时用于督验转运的签押。
温梨拿着那张票，指腹沿着父亲的名字摸了一遍。
“是真的。”她说。
我看了看她：“你怎么确定？”
“这是他的字。”
李氏却从她手里抽回纸：“看着像，不能作数。旁人照着字样也能描。要证实这是不是他签的，还得核对当时的登记，让他本人说明。”
这句话把我吓了一跳。
不是她多谨慎，而是她似乎早想过这些凭证有一天会被拿出来审。
“那后头的腊月初九呢？”我问。
母亲将一张收货凭单摊在旁边。纸张发黄，正中写着‘官仓实收三千石’，下面却没落正式收粮官的姓名，只盖了一枚模糊的仓印。
“八千石运出去，官仓只收三千？”
“我只知道宋账房带回来的这张纸写三千。”母亲说，“是不是实收三千，要找当年的仓册。五千石究竟去了哪里，这张纸回答不了。”
她把那封旧信交给我。
宋账房的字有些歪，写的是船队抵达后有人让他把剩下的粮另作登记，他不肯，便被告知‘只管领脚钱，不要多问’。信的最后几行几乎写不下去，说有人在打听他的孙子。
我读到那里，想起春桃一路拉着我跑的样子。
书里一句‘旧案’，落在这些人身上，原来是不能睡安稳的三年。
“您报过官吗？”我问。
“宋账房去过县衙。”母亲说，“回来的时候脸上带着伤。第二次他要去府衙，我没让。”
“为什么不让？”
“因为他孙子那时才六岁。”
她说得很硬，却将信纸压平了两次。
温梨一直没有接话。她听到这里才低声说：“我爹就是因为那年的事，第二年入秋被押走，案子后来才送到刑部。”
“他和这事是什么关系？”我问。
“官府说他督验失职，后来又拿出一张入仓单，说八千石全数入仓是他签字确认的。那五千石的去向，就这样算到了他头上。”
“那张写着八千石全数入仓的单子，他究竟签没签？”
温梨看了我一眼，像是没想到我会这样问。
“签过。”她说，“我爹承认那张单子上有他的签名，但他说不是自愿签的。”
“可签了就是签了。”李氏打断她，“他为什么签，得由他自己说清楚。”
温梨低头：“我明白。”
我以为她会替父亲争辩，没想到她一声都没多说。
空气闷得我坐不住，便去翻那本流水账。翻过两页，发现里面的数字比官仓凭单还奇怪。
“娘，怎么有两笔脚钱？”
第一笔是商号雇船运粮的正常费用；第二笔没有写船号，只在旁边标了个小小的‘另’字。
母亲伸手合上账册。
“这笔先别动。”
我一怔。
“为什么？”
“因为我还没想好该怎么告诉你。”
她没有再解释，连温梨也识趣地没问。我却记住了那一页的位置。母亲担心姜家担责，绝不是没有原因。
温梨取出随身记下的侯府账目，指着腊月初九的日期，又点了点姜家的船票：“至少这两处日期对不上。但还不能断定记的是同一趟船。接下来得查东平码头的出航簿，再找官仓当年的收粮人。”
“这种旧簿子还会在吗？”我问。
“看是谁管的。”母亲说，“宋账房信里提过严满仓。北河旧仓的看仓人，他也许知道那五千石去了哪里。”
我立刻起身：“那现在就找他！”
母亲瞟我一眼：“你知道他住哪儿？”
“不知道。”
“你知道他还活着？”
“不知道。”
“你知道外头是谁在盯姜府？”
“……这个也不知道。”
“那就坐下。”
我只好坐回去。
温梨低着头，肩膀轻轻一抖。
“你笑什么？”我问。
“没笑。”
“你都快笑出声了！”
“我只是觉得，姜夫人说得很对。”
我看向母亲求援，母亲却把茶盏往我面前一推：“喝水。你今天说话说得够多了。”
这两个人什么时候站到一边去了？
到了傍晚，我们没有直接去找严满仓，而是先去了姜府往来多年的脚行。
母亲派老管事秦叔陪同。他带着当年的雇船名录，说要先从船工家属那里问起。
我本来还想着能不能靠一袋银子买下消息，秦叔一句话就把我按回现实：“姑娘，若谢家也在找这个人，您拿银子砸出去，第二天满城都会知道您要找谁。”
“那怎么办？”
“先找他当年用过的行号，再问那家的老伙计。只说要补结旧工钱。”
温梨看了我一眼：“学着点。”
我不服：“我出的是钱，你出的是嘴，凭什么你教我？”
“因为钱太响了。”
我没忍住笑，笑完又有点心虚。她倒是把我刚才没考虑的危险说清楚了。
脚行里有两名老伙计。一人说严满仓去年已经离开北河，另一人说见过他在城南岑记脚行讨活，只是不知道还在不在。
秦叔默默记下线索，门外卖糖人的孩子却不小心把竹签掉在我脚边。
我正想弯腰捡，温梨按住我手腕。
街对面站着两个男人，穿普通短打，衣服却新得不像跑脚行的，眼神一刻不离我们这边。
“谢家的人？”我低声问。
“可能。”温梨说，“但还不能确定。”
温梨弯腰替孩子捡起竹签，顺手买了个糖人，若无其事地递给我。那两个男人见我们没继续往外走，便慢慢分开，一人朝北，一人守在巷口。
“现在怎么办？”我问。
“回去。”
“严满仓不找了？”
“找。”温梨看了看秦叔手里的地址，“换个人去找。我们要是现在奔城南，他们就知道严满仓在哪儿了。”
我想起自己穿来第一刻就想靠‘知道剧情’解决所有问题，突然有些羞愧。这个世界里的每个人都只能凭手头的消息做选择，温梨也一样。
回到姜府，门房递给我一张烫金帖子。
谢临舟亲笔写的。
明日午时，侯府花厅一叙。带姜记旧账。
末尾还添了一句：不要再信温梨。
我看着那一行字，抬头问母亲：“他说带旧账。”
母亲没有接帖子，只问：“他怎么知道我手上还有？”
这回，连温梨都不笑了。
原来我们在屋里关起门来藏了半天的秘密，早就有人替我们数好了。

annotations.meaning: 惊天动地的；影响巨大的
annotations.explain: 常用于形容重大消息或发现，也可与 news、revelation 搭配。
annotations.example: It wasn't exactly earth-shattering news.

annotations.explain: fall apart 可指物件损坏，也可引申为计划崩溃、情绪失控。
annotations.example: The old book was falling apart.

annotations.phrase: It wasn't much to look at
annotations.explain: not much to look at 指外观普通，不能据此判断实际价值。
annotations.example: The house isn't much to look at, but it's comfortable.

annotations.explain: 句首 Still 表示转折，可译为“不过、尽管如此”，不表示“仍然”这一时间意义。
annotations.example: It was late. Still, we kept going.

annotations.explain: have + 人 + 动词原形 表示安排或使某人做事。
annotations.example: She had the clerk check the records.

annotations.explain: be bound for + 地点 表示正前往某处，多用于车辆、船只、货物。
annotations.example: The train is bound for Osaka.

annotations.explain: bore 是 bear 的过去式；在书面语中 bear a seal/signature 意为“盖有印章/带有签名”。
annotations.example: The document bore his signature.

annotations.explain: 比直接断言更谨慎，用于证据尚待验证的场合。
annotations.example: We found what appeared to be an old map.

annotations.explain: along with 用来补充随附信息，通常比 and 更突出前一项。
annotations.example: The package came with a note, along with a receipt.

annotations.explain: trace + 名词 可以表示手指沿轮廓慢慢移动，不一定是查找来源。
annotations.example: She traced the letters on the stone.

annotations.phrase: with the pad of her thumb
annotations.explain: the pad of a finger 是手指柔软的指腹；这是常见文学动作描写。
annotations.example: He touched the glass with the pad of his finger.

annotations.explain: genuine 多用来判断文件、物件或感情的真实性。
annotations.example: Is this signature genuine?

annotations.explain: 询问判断依据，不是单纯表达不信任。
annotations.example: How can you be sure it was him?

annotations.explain: That doesn't make ... 常用于指出某一事实不能自动推出另一结论。
annotations.example: He's confident, but that doesn't make him right.

annotations.explain: would have to 常表示假设条件下有必要做的事，语气比直接命令缓和。
annotations.example: We'd have to check the dates first.

annotations.phrase: hear what he has to say
annotations.explain: hear what sb has to say 指让当事人陈述意见，不预设其说法正确。
annotations.example: Let's hear what she has to say.

annotations.explain: Not because A, but because B 用来纠正读者可能误判的原因。
annotations.example: I left, not because I was angry, but because I was tired.

annotations.explain: possibility that 后接完整从句说明是什么可能发生。
annotations.example: We discussed the possibility that the train was delayed.

annotations.explain: might + one day 表示不确定的未来可能性。
annotations.example: This letter might one day matter.

annotations.phrase: spread a delivery receipt beside it
annotations.explain: spread sth out 指将纸张、地图等展开摆放以供查看。
annotations.example: He spread the map across the table.

annotations.explain: had + 过去分词 表示在叙述过去时点之前已经形成的状态。
annotations.example: The pages had yellowed with age.

annotations.explain: across 可表示“横过某表面”，在描述文字、痕迹位置时很常见。
annotations.example: A dark line ran across the page.

annotations.explain: beneath 比 under 更常出现在书面描写，指位置在下方。
annotations.example: Her name was printed beneath the title.

annotations.explain: All I know is (that) ... 用于主动限定自己知道的事实范围。
annotations.example: All I know is that he left early.

annotations.meaning: 至于是否……则是另一回事
annotations.explain: 用于区分“文件怎么写”和“事实是否如此”等不同命题。
annotations.example: Whether it will work is another matter.

annotations.explain: would need 常用于假设推演、提出必要条件。
annotations.example: We'd need more evidence to prove it.

annotations.explain: scrap of paper 表示一小张纸，常暗示单薄或零碎。
annotations.example: She wrote the address on a scrap of paper.

annotations.explain: crooked 描述不直的文字、道路，也可形容不诚实的人；此处只指笔迹。
annotations.example: His handwriting was crooked.

annotations.explain: under + 类别或名目 表示“归入某项之下”。
annotations.example: The expense was filed under travel.

annotations.explain: stop + doing 表示停止正在做的动作；不同于 stop to do（停下来去做）。
annotations.example: Stop asking questions and listen.

annotations.explain: give out 可形容机器、体力、声音或笔力衰竭。
annotations.example: Her voice gave out near the end.

annotations.explain: reach a part / passage 可表示阅读推进到某处。
annotations.example: I cried when I reached the final chapter.

annotations.explain: drag sb along 带有拉拽或催促意味，比 lead sb 更急切。
annotations.example: He dragged his friend along to the station.

annotations.explain: be caught up in 常表示不由自主地卷入麻烦、冲突、事件。
annotations.example: They got caught up in the dispute.

annotations.explain: mean 后接实际后果，有时比字面定义更重要。
annotations.example: For her, failure meant losing her home.

annotations.explain: sleep soundly 是常见搭配；soundly 在这里表示“熟睡”，不是“发出声音”。
annotations.example: I haven't slept soundly in weeks.

annotations.explain: report sth to sb 为固定结构，表示向有职责的人报告某事。
annotations.example: They reported the theft to the police.

annotations.explain: come back with + 结果/物品 可表示回来时带回了什么。
annotations.example: He came back with a broken arm.

annotations.explain: take a case/complaint to an authority 表示将事件交给更高层处理。
annotations.example: She decided to take the complaint to court.

annotations.explain: only 放在数字前可以突出年纪太小、数量不足的说话人态度。
annotations.example: The child was only six.

annotations.explain: firm voice/tone 描述坚定而非大声。
annotations.example: She answered in a firm voice.

annotations.explain: smooth sth flat 是“使某物变得平整”的结果性表达。
annotations.example: He smoothed the cloth flat.

annotations.explain: until then 表示延续到叙述的那个时间点为止。
annotations.example: She had said nothing until then.

annotations.explain: at last 强调经过等待或沉默之后终于发生。
annotations.example: At last, the door opened.

annotations.explain: pass sth up to 表示递交给上一级部门/负责人，此处是案件移送。
annotations.example: The report was passed up to the director.

annotations.explain: accuse sb of + 名词或 doing 为常见固定搭配。
annotations.example: They accused him of hiding the records.

annotations.explain: supposedly 暗示说法尚未独立证实。
annotations.example: The letter was supposedly signed by the mayor.

annotations.explain: end up + doing/being done 描述事情最后发展成的结果；blame ... on sb 表示归咎于某人。
annotations.example: The mistake ended up being blamed on me.

annotations.explain: But did he ...? 在对话中用于追问关键事实，与先前说法形成对比。
annotations.example: But did he actually see it?

annotations.explain: as though 后接从句，可描写主观印象，不等于确认事实。
annotations.example: She stared at me as though I'd lost my mind.

annotations.explain: admit + 名词或 that 从句；通常暗含事实对本人不利。
annotations.example: He admitted that the signature was his.

annotations.explain: 固定表达，强调未受胁迫。
annotations.example: She signed it of her own free will.

annotations.phrase: A signature is still a signature
annotations.explain: A is still A 强调即使有其他情况，核心事实仍在；语气坚定。
annotations.example: A promise is still a promise.

annotations.explain: cut in 表示插话或中途打断，常见于小说对白标记。
annotations.example: "Wait," she cut in.

annotations.explain: put one's name to sth 表示签署并承担一定责任。
annotations.example: He refused to put his name to the statement.

annotations.explain: 过去完成式表示当时此前形成的预期，后文通常与实际结果形成反差。
annotations.example: I'd expected her to complain, but she smiled.

annotations.explain: instead 引出与前面预期相反的实际结果。
annotations.example: I expected an apology. Instead, he laughed.

annotations.explain: too + 形容词 + to do 表示“太……以至于不能……”。
annotations.example: The room was too hot to sleep in.

annotations.explain: X pages/chapters in 表示阅读进行到某个位置。
annotations.example: Ten pages in, I knew I loved the book.

annotations.explain: payment for + 事项 表示因什么而支付的钱。
annotations.example: The company made a payment for repairs.

annotations.explain: 否定句中的 at all 用于加强否定语气。
annotations.example: There was no reference number at all.

annotations.explain: reach across 表示将手臂伸到另一侧。
annotations.example: He reached across the table for the book.

annotations.explain: for now 是暂时性安排，含以后可能再处理的意味。
annotations.example: Let's leave it alone for now.

annotations.explain: freeze 在叙事中可指因震惊或害怕突然僵住，不一定涉及寒冷。
annotations.example: I froze when I heard my name.

annotations.explain: work out 可表示想出办法、理清思路，而非只指锻炼。
annotations.example: I haven't worked out what to say.

annotations.explain: further + 名词 表示额外、进一步的信息。
annotations.example: He offered no further details.

annotations.explain: have the sense to do 表示有判断力去做某事；否定不定式表示克制不做。
annotations.example: She had the sense not to argue.

annotations.explain: press sb 在此表示继续施压追问，而不是按压。
annotations.example: Don't press him for an answer yet.

annotations.explain: come from nowhere 原指突然出现；否定表达强调有其原因。
annotations.example: Her concern hadn't come from nowhere.

annotations.explain: take out 表示从某处取出；take out notes 是常见叙事动作。
annotations.example: She took out a folded note.

annotations.explain: 表示最低限度可以确定或要求的内容，常用于谨慎结论。
annotations.example: At the very least, we should check the dates.

annotations.explain: match 在这里指记录中的信息相符，不是比赛。
annotations.example: The names on the forms don't match.

annotations.explain: can't say 表示证据不足以断言，区别于“不允许说”。
annotations.example: We can't say the two reports refer to one event.

annotations.explain: refer to + 人/事物 表示所指对象，也可表示查阅。
annotations.example: These numbers refer to last year's sales.

annotations.explain: next 在句首承担叙事/计划顺序功能。
annotations.example: Next we need to find the original file.

annotations.explain: would 用来推测或委婉提出不确定疑问。
annotations.example: Would records from that year still exist?

annotations.explain: 固定表达，后接名词或疑问词从句。
annotations.example: That depends on who you ask.

annotations.explain: might 表示不确定可能性；与肯定陈述作区分。
annotations.example: She might know where the key is.

annotations.explain: spring to one's feet 是小说里常见的突然起身动作。
annotations.example: He sprang to his feet at the news.

annotations.explain: give sb a sideways look 常暗示怀疑、不赞同或无奈。
annotations.example: My mother gave me a sideways look.

annotations.explain: even 在此表示连最基本或意想不到的条件都未知。
annotations.example: We don't know if he's even alive.

annotations.explain: watch 可指监视，不只是观看。
annotations.example: Someone had been watching the house.

annotations.explain: give a shake 是动词+名词构成的动作表达，此处表现憋笑。
annotations.example: His shoulders gave a little shake.

annotations.explain: burst out + doing 表示突然开始某动作，常见 burst out laughing/crying。
annotations.example: She burst out laughing at the joke.

annotations.explain: make a point 是“提出观点”，make a good point 指观点有说服力。
annotations.example: You make a good point about safety.

annotations.explain: turn to sb for + 名词 表示向某人寻求帮助、建议、支持。
annotations.example: I turned to her for advice.

annotations.explain: quite + enough 可强化“足够了/该停了”的语气。
annotations.example: You've done quite enough for today.

annotations.explain: Since when + 助动词/倒装，常用于惊讶或不满的反问。
annotations.example: Since when did you become the expert?

annotations.explain: be on the same side 指立场一致，不一定实际站在同一位置。
annotations.example: For once, we're on the same side.

annotations.explain: by + 时间点 表示不晚于该时间或到了该时间时形成的情况。
annotations.example: By evening, the rain had stopped.

annotations.explain: instead 用于否定原计划后引出实际行动。
annotations.example: We didn't call him. Instead, we sent a letter.

annotations.explain: send sb with us 表示安排某人同行。
annotations.example: They sent a guide with us.

annotations.explain: start by + doing 表示采取某动作作为第一步。
annotations.example: Start by checking the date.

annotations.explain: 描述货币量的具象说法，有古风背景，非现代纸币。
annotations.example: He offered a bag of coins.

annotations.explain: buy sb sth 表示“为某人买/换来某物”，此处隐含贿买消息。
annotations.example: Money won't buy you trust.

annotations.phrase: brought me firmly back to earth
annotations.explain: bring sb back to earth 指让人从空想恢复现实判断。
annotations.example: The cost brought us back to earth.

annotations.explain: throw money around 含炫耀或不审慎地用钱的意味。
annotations.example: Stop throwing money around.

annotations.explain: be after sb 可表示追寻、寻找某人，不一定是攻击。
annotations.example: Who are you after?

annotations.explain: work through an agency 表示通过中介/机构获得工作。
annotations.example: He found work through an agency.

annotations.explain: old hand 是有经验的人，而不指年纪大的手。
annotations.example: Ask one of the old hands.

annotations.explain: settle a debt/bill/wages 表示结算并处理欠款。
annotations.example: The company settled the unpaid wages.

annotations.explain: 固定口语，略带调侃，暗示对方有值得学习的地方。
annotations.example: You could learn a thing or two from her.

annotations.meaning: 我不服气；我一下子恼了
annotations.explain: bristle 描写对批评或挑衅立即产生的防御/恼怒反应。
annotations.example: She bristled at the accusation.

annotations.explain: get to do 可表示有机会/权利做某事，此句是在质疑资格。
annotations.example: Why do you get to decide?

annotations.explain: 此处是隐喻：大笔银子会让找人的行动暴露，不是钱真的发声。
annotations.example: A big reward would make too much noise.

annotations.explain: can't/couldn't help + doing 表示无法克制某个反应。
annotations.example: I couldn't help smiling.

annotations.meaning: 准确指出；抓住问题关键
annotations.explain: put one's finger on sth 表示明确说中某个问题。
annotations.example: She put her finger on the real problem.

annotations.explain: 过去完成时表示在该叙述时点之前未曾考虑；even 强化遗漏程度。
annotations.example: I hadn't even considered that risk.

annotations.explain: look for work 是常见表达；work 在此不可数，指工作机会。
annotations.example: He's been looking for work.

annotations.explain: still 强调状态持续未变化。
annotations.example: I don't know if he is still there.

annotations.explain: commit sth to memory 是正式表达，指认真记住；lead 作名词为线索。
annotations.example: She committed the address to memory.

annotations.explain: by 在此表示靠近、在旁边。
annotations.example: The note fell by my chair.

annotations.explain: be about to + 动词原形 表示即将做某事。
annotations.example: I was about to leave when she called.

annotations.explain: catch sb's wrist/arm 表示突然抓住阻止动作。
annotations.example: He caught my arm before I fell.

annotations.explain: across 表示横跨到另一侧；与 along the street（沿街）不同。
annotations.example: There's a shop across the street.

annotations.explain: suspiciously + 形容词 表示某种程度引人怀疑。
annotations.example: The document looked suspiciously new.

annotations.phrase: Neither took his eyes off us
annotations.meaning: 两个人都一直盯着我们
annotations.explain: not take one's eyes off sb = 目不转睛地盯着某人；neither 指两者都不。
annotations.example: He never took his eyes off the door.

annotations.explain: whisper 表示压低声音讲话，适合隐蔽观察情境。
annotations.example: "Look over there," she whispered.

annotations.explain: 单独回答 Possibly 比 Yes 更保留判断空间。
annotations.example: "Is it true?" "Possibly."

annotations.explain: as though + 过去式/虚拟式 描写与真实紧张情况相反的表面姿态。
annotations.example: She smiled as though nothing were wrong.

annotations.explain: split up 可指人群分散、情侣分手；此处是两人分头走。
annotations.example: We split up to search the building.

annotations.phrase: at the mouth of the alley
annotations.explain: mouth 可比喻河口、洞口、巷口等开口位置。
annotations.example: A guard stood at the mouth of the tunnel.

annotations.explain: give up on sb/sth 表示不再尝试或指望。
annotations.example: Don't give up on finding her.

annotations.explain: head + 方向 表示朝某方向前进，straight 强调没有绕路。
annotations.example: They headed straight home.

annotations.phrase: lead those men right to him
annotations.meaning: 把那些人直接引到他那里
annotations.explain: lead sb to sb/sth 表示把人带到某处；right 强调正好、直接。
annotations.example: You'll lead them right to us.

annotations.explain: think back to sth 指回忆过去的某时刻。
annotations.example: I thought back to our first meeting.

annotations.explain: assume that 是未经充分证实而作出假设，与 know 区分。
annotations.example: I assumed that she had left.

annotations.meaning: 凭手头能得到的消息作决定
annotations.explain: whatever + 名词 表示“无论什么/凡是可得到的”，强调信息有限。
annotations.example: We worked with whatever tools we had.

annotations.explain: no different 表示情况同样适用，不是说人物相同。
annotations.example: She was no different from the rest of us.

annotations.explain: edge 作动词可描述边缘装饰或镶边。
annotations.example: The invitation was edged in silver.

annotations.explain: in sb's own hand 指亲笔书写，不是拿在手里。
annotations.example: The note was in her own hand.

annotations.phrase: Bring the Jiang Trading House's old accounts
annotations.explain: 祈使句省略主语 you，可体现邀请帖中强势的要求口吻。
annotations.example: Bring the documents tomorrow.

annotations.explain: at the bottom of a page/letter 表示页面最下方。
annotations.example: He signed at the bottom.

annotations.explain: look up at 表示从低处向上看；不同于 look up（查阅）。
annotations.example: She looked up at her mother.

annotations.explain: reach for sth 表示伸手取某物，动作缺席可体现态度。
annotations.example: He didn't reach for the letter.

annotations.explain: still have 强调原本可能已交出/处理的物件仍被保留。
annotations.example: Do you still have the receipt?

annotations.explain: not even 强调出乎意料的例外也没有发生。
annotations.example: Not even he knew the answer.

annotations.explain: behind closed doors 可字面关门，也常比喻私下秘密商议。
annotations.example: They met behind closed doors.

annotations.explain: Apparently 表示根据目前迹象推断，语气不同于 certainly。
annotations.example: Apparently, someone had heard us.

annotations.explain: all along 表示某事从早先就持续存在，常用于真相揭露时。
annotations.example: She had known all along.

scenes.title: 木匣打开
scenes.alt: 烛光下，李氏打开木匣，露出旧船票、凭单、信件和薄账，姜明月与温梨俯身查看。

scenes.title: 核对签押
scenes.alt: 李氏与温梨在暖灯下比对旧凭证，姜明月紧张地盯着纸上签押与日期。

scenes.title: 宋账房旧信
scenes.alt: 姜明月读着宋账房留下的旧信，神色愈发不安，温梨与李氏在一旁沉思。

scenes.title: 另一笔脚钱
scenes.alt: 三人围着桌上的账册继续查对，意外翻出另一笔可疑的运费记录。

scenes.title: 脚行访旧工
scenes.alt: 黄昏的脚行里，秦叔向老伙计打听旧雇船线索，姜明月和温梨在旁凝神听着。

scenes.title: 街头疑似尾随
scenes.alt: 热闹街市旁，温梨轻按住姜明月的手臂，远处两名男子回头张望，前景有举着糖人的孩童。

scenes.title: 烫金帖子
scenes.alt: 回府后的暖灯下，姜明月捧着谢临舟送来的烫金请帖，温梨与李氏神情沉重。
